pageProps.title: The Rules of a Great Detective
pageProps.review: A self-confessing novel by Keigo Higashino that satirizes the trite clichés of existing mystery novels and newly declares his literary orientation through a unique meta-fiction technique that breaks the fourth wall.
pageProps.description: A blade of criticism wrapped in a bundle of laughter
pageProps.content:
## Review It is close to a self-confessing novel that breaks away from the conventions of the mystery novel genre. The main characters of the work are aware that they are characters in a novel. They constantly break the ```fourth wall``` and complain about the author's laziness, trite plots, and old clichés they are forced to act out.
If the author's early works focused on puzzle-solving, they tended to focus on human relationships and criminal motives after this work. This work seems to be a public manifesto for his literary direction.
The detective who reluctantly acts like a genius and the character who plays the role of a self-aware fool are impressive.
